open_points.subject: Client-viewer administration authority
open_points.text: “For an active project an operator can … manage client viewers, access links, and project grants” contradicts R0-14: “Creating, revoking and re-issuing client viewers, their access links and project grants … all require the access-management capability, which only administrators hold.”
open_points.question: Can an operator manage viewers, links, or grants, or are all of those actions administrator-only?
options: Operators may perform these actions for assigned projects
Only administrators may perform these actions
open_points.default_guess: Only administrators may perform them, following R0-14.

witness.initial: An operator is assigned to active project P and has no access-management capability.
events: The operator requests creation of a viewer grant for P.
outcomes: The request succeeds under “Operator management.”
The request is denied under R0-14.
witness.observer: The operator and the audit reader

open_points.subject: Actor that creates a ClientViewer
open_points.text: ClientViewer is “created by an operator,” while R0-14 says creating client viewers requires a capability “which only administrators hold.”
open_points.question: Does “operator” here mean the operator role, any staff actor, or specifically an administrator?
options: The operator role may create a viewer
Only an administrator may create a viewer
“Operator” is a generic term including administrators
open_points.default_guess: Only an administrator may create a viewer.

witness.initial: An authenticated staff account has role operator and is assigned to project P.
events: The staff member submits the viewer-creation action.
outcomes: Creation succeeds because the principal section names an operator.
Creation is forbidden because R0-14 reserves it to administrators.

open_points.subject: Service-principal authorization
open_points.text: “Every project-scoped operation checks together: valid active session” conflicts with service principals authenticating “only with a bearer header” and having credentials but no defined session.
open_points.question: Is a service-principal bearer credential itself sufficient for project-scoped import operations, or must it create or accompany a session?
options: Bearer authentication is an explicit exception to the session requirement
Bearer authentication creates a service-principal session
Service principals must supply both bearer credential and session
open_points.default_guess: Treat bearer authentication as an explicit exception to the session requirement.

witness.initial: An active producer is scoped to project P and holds a valid bearer credential.
events: The producer publishes a snapshot for P without a session token.
outcomes: The import succeeds under R0-09 and R0-15.
The import fails because the common rule requires an active session.

open_points.subject: Role and capability definitions
open_points.text: “Roles map to closed capability sets” and “required capability” are stated, but the closed sets and capability identifiers are not listed except for two service-principal capabilities and access management.
open_points.question: What is the complete capability set, which role receives each capability, and which action requires which capability?
options: Define one capability per action or action family
Use broad mutation, read, and access-management capabilities
Defer capability checks to route-specific implementation choices
open_points.default_guess: Define explicit read, project-mutation, activation, and access-management capabilities and map every action to one.

witness.initial: An operator is assigned to project P.
events: The operator attempts snapshot activation for P.
outcomes: Activation succeeds because it is listed under operator management.
Activation is denied because an implementer treats activation as an administrative capability.

open_points.subject: Staff-session transport
open_points.text: Staff accounts have “managed sessions,” but only viewer-cookie and producer-bearer transport are specified.
open_points.question: How is a staff session issued and transported on HTTP requests, and what origin or CSRF protections apply?
options: Host-only secure HTTP-only cookie
Bearer token in an authorization header
A distinct staff-session transport defined later
open_points.default_guess: Use a host-only secure HTTP-only same-site cookie with explicit origin/CSRF checks for mutations.

witness.initial: A staff member has successfully logged in.
events: A browser calls a project mutation using only the session cookie.
Another client calls it using only an Authorization bearer value.
outcomes: Only the cookie request is authenticated.
Only the bearer request is authenticated.

open_points.subject: Staff-account lifecycle
open_points.text: The text names “pending_verification,” active accounts, suspension, and disabling, but does not define their transitions, who may perform each transition, or whether suspension and disabling are reversible.
open_points.question: What are the staff-account states and permitted state-changing actions, including reactivation or re-enabling?
options: Suspension is reversible and disabling is permanent
Both suspension and disabling are reversible but have different policy meanings
Use one inactive state despite the two terms
open_points.default_guess: Model pending_verification, active, suspended, and disabled, with administrator-only explicit transitions and disabled treated as terminal.

witness.initial: A verified active staff account is suspended by an administrator.
events: The administrator later attempts to restore the account.
outcomes: The account can be reactivated and can log in again.
No restoration action exists, so the account remains blocked permanently.

open_points.subject: Service-credential rotation overlap
open_points.text: Credentials are “rotatable with an overlap period,” but no duration, start/end rule, or action for ending overlap is defined.
open_points.question: How is the overlap period determined, and when exactly does the old credential stop authenticating?
options: A fixed configured duration after rotation
An expiry selected during rotation
Both credentials remain valid until explicit revocation
open_points.default_guess: Use a deployment-configured fixed overlap duration beginning when the replacement is issued.

witness.initial: Producer credential A is active.
events: An administrator rotates A and receives credential B.
The producer uses A one hour later.
outcomes: A remains accepted during an implementation-chosen overlap.
A was revoked immediately and the request is rejected.

open_points.subject: Viewer access-link issuance result
open_points.text: A ViewerAccessCredential is “issued and re-issuable by an operator,” “shown” behavior is not stated, and it is stored only in verification form.
open_points.question: Which actor receives the one recoverable access URL or secret, through what action result, and what happens if that result is lost?
options: Return the access URL exactly once in the issuance response
Deliver it through a named external channel
Allow the issuer to retrieve it later despite verification-only storage
open_points.default_guess: Return it exactly once to the authorized administrator and require re-issuance if lost.

witness.initial: A viewer exists without a usable access link.
events: An administrator issues a credential.
The response is lost before the administrator copies it.
outcomes: The credential can be retrieved later.
It cannot be recovered and must be re-issued, revoking the just-issued credential.

open_points.subject: Viewer session restoration
open_points.text: “Viewers can restore and end their session explicitly.”
open_points.question: What does restore mean, what input authorizes it, and what observable result or failure does the restore action have?
options: Re-enter through the current access link to create a new session
Refresh an existing unexpired session
Restore a revoked or expired session through another credential
open_points.default_guess: Interpret restore as re-entering with the current access link to create a fresh fixed-expiry session.

witness.initial: A viewer has a valid access credential but no session cookie.
events: The viewer invokes the restore operation without presenting the access credential.
outcomes: A session is restored from another browser-held value.
The request fails because entry with the access credential is required.

open_points.subject: Activation with unmapped expenses
open_points.text: “Unmapped expenses stay visible and must be resolved by an operator,” but the text does not say whether activation may complete while such expenses exist.
open_points.question: Must every existing allocation be mapped before a new budget version can be activated?
options: Block activation until all mappings are resolved
Allow activation and expose allocations as unmapped
Allow activation but exclude unmapped amounts from section totals
open_points.default_guess: Allow activation with explicitly visible unmapped allocations, because the text says they stay visible after the transition.

witness.initial: Project P has an active manual budget and an included expense allocated to section M, which has no correspondence in imported version V.
events: An operator activates V without supplying a mapping for M.
outcomes: Activation is rejected until M is mapped.
V becomes active and the expense remains visible as unmapped.

open_points.subject: Work progress across budget changes
open_points.text: The transition rules preserve and map expenses and explicitly preserve payments and photos, but do not state what happens to “work progress per section” when a new budget version is activated.
open_points.question: How is existing section progress carried, mapped, reset, or retained when the active budget changes?
options: Map progress by stable section correspondence
Keep progress attached only to the old budget version
Reset progress for all sections in the new version
Require manual progress mapping before activation
open_points.default_guess: Carry progress only through explicit stable-section mapping and leave unmatched progress attached to the old version.

witness.initial: Manual section M is at 60% completion; imported version V contains corresponding section S.
events: An operator activates V.
outcomes: S appears at 60% through the section mapping.
S appears with unavailable or zero progress while M retains 60% only in history.

open_points.subject: Photo section association across budget changes
open_points.text: “Payments and photos do not depend on budget version changes,” while photos may have a “section association”; the persistence or remapping of that association is not defined.
open_points.question: What section association is displayed for a photo after its associated section is replaced by a new active budget version?
options: Map the association to the corresponding new section
Retain the historical old-section association
Remove the association when the old section is no longer active
open_points.default_guess: Retain the historical association and optionally expose a mapped current section when an explicit mapping exists.

witness.initial: Photo F is associated with manual section M.
events: Imported version V is activated and M maps to S.
A viewer opens F.
outcomes: F is shown under S.
F remains associated with M or appears unassociated.

open_points.subject: Stable section-identifier correspondence
open_points.text: “Matching stable section identifiers may link automatically,” but manual section identifiers, producer source identifiers, estimate identities, and producers have no defined shared namespace.
open_points.question: Which identifiers are comparable across manual and imported versions, and what scope prevents collisions between projects, estimates, or producers?
options: Only explicit operator-approved mappings link different source namespaces
Equal source_section_id values link within one estimate lineage
Equal identifiers link globally across all budget sources
open_points.default_guess: Automatically link only within a declared estimate lineage and require explicit mapping across manual or producer namespaces.

witness.initial: Manual section M and imported section S both have textual identifier “1”, but were created independently.
events: Version V containing S is activated.
outcomes: M and S are linked automatically because their identifiers match.
They remain unmapped because their identifiers are from different namespaces.

open_points.subject: Approved-snapshot identity scope
open_points.text: “Snapshot identity is estimate_id + estimate_version for one project_id.”
open_points.question: Is estimate_id + estimate_version globally unique, unique per project, or unique per producer and project?
options: Global pair: estimate_id + estimate_version
Project-scoped triple: project_id + estimate_id + estimate_version
Producer- and project-scoped identity
open_points.default_guess: Use project_id + producer identity + estimate_id + estimate_version.

witness.initial: Producer A has imported estimate E version 1 for project P1.
events: The same producer imports estimate E version 1 for project P2.
outcomes: The second import is an identity conflict.
The second import creates a distinct snapshot under P2.

open_points.subject: Snapshot content equality and fingerprint
open_points.text: “Identical content” is idempotent and a “content fingerprint” is recorded, but the canonical content, ordering rules, and normalization used for equality are not defined.
open_points.question: Which fields and canonicalization determine whether a replay is identical?
options: Fingerprint the exact received JSON bytes
Fingerprint a canonicalized contract payload including section order
Fingerprint only business fields and ignore provenance or publication metadata
open_points.default_guess: Fingerprint a contract-version-specific canonical representation of all accepted payload fields, preserving semantic section order.

witness.initial: Snapshot E/1 was accepted with amount 10.00 and one JSON field order.
events: The producer replays E/1 with amount 10.0 and different object-key order but identical business meaning.
outcomes: The replay is idempotent after canonicalization.
The replay is rejected as different content because the bytes differ.

open_points.subject: Manual section removal and existing records
open_points.text: An operator may “maintain the manual budget,” but no rule states whether a section referenced by allocations, progress, or photos may be removed or reordered, or what replaces it.
open_points.question: What actions are permitted on a referenced manual section, and what happens to its dependent records?
options: Referenced sections cannot be deleted
Deletion archives the section and preserves all references
Deletion requires explicit remapping of every dependent record
open_points.default_guess: Use stable archived sections and forbid destructive deletion while references exist.

witness.initial: Manual section M has an included allocation, progress, and a visible photo.
events: An operator removes M while maintaining the manual budget.
outcomes: Removal is rejected because M is referenced.
M disappears and its dependent records become unmapped, hidden, or invalid.

open_points.subject: Unavailable client data
open_points.text: “Unavailable data is shown explicitly, never fabricated or replaced by silent zeros.”
open_points.question: For each client-view field, what conditions make it unavailable and what JSON representation distinguishes unavailable, zero, omitted, forbidden, and external-system failure?
options: Use null plus a machine-readable reason
Omit unavailable fields
Return a typed unavailable object or error
open_points.default_guess: Return null with a closed machine-readable unavailability reason while preserving genuine numeric zero.

witness.initial: Project P has no planned work cost.
events: A viewer requests overall progress.
outcomes: The response contains null with an unavailable reason.
The field is omitted or the entire request fails.

open_points.subject: Authenticity of confirmed OCR results
open_points.text: The portal “accepts only the versioned confirmed normalized recognition contract,” but R0-17 says an authenticated staff member submits that result; no OCR principal, signature, lookup, or other proof binds the submitted content to OCR.
open_points.question: How does the portal establish that operator-submitted recognition content is the confirmed output of the OCR service rather than staff-supplied data?
options: Trust authorized staff to relay the result without cryptographic proof
Require an OCR-issued signed assertion
Have the portal retrieve the confirmed result by recognized_document_id
Give OCR its own service principal and publication action
open_points.default_guess: Require a verifiable OCR-issued assertion or authenticated lookup keyed by recognized_document_id.

witness.initial: An operator has mutation capability on project P but OCR has produced no confirmed document D.
events: The operator submits a syntactically valid confirmed-result payload claiming identifier D.
outcomes: The portal creates an Expense because staff authority is sufficient.
The portal rejects it because no authenticated OCR confirmation exists.

open_points.subject: Expense-intake replay conflict
open_points.text: “One recognized document creates at most one Expense with one Document; replay is idempotent,” but behavior for the same recognized_document_id with different project, content, total, document reference, or allocation is not stated.
open_points.question: Which fields must match for an idempotent replay, and what explicit failure occurs when they differ?
options: Return the existing expense regardless of payload differences
Reject any differing replay as an integrity conflict
Treat allocation differences as an authorized update while other differences conflict
open_points.default_guess: Return the existing result only for an identical canonical request and reject any differing replay as an integrity conflict.

witness.initial: Recognized document D created expense E in project P1.
events: A staff member replays D with project P2 and a different total.
outcomes: The existing E is returned as an idempotent replay.
The request is rejected as a conflicting replay.

open_points.subject: Payment idempotency conflict
open_points.text: Work payments are “idempotent by stable payment identity,” but identity scope and behavior for a repeated identity with different amount, date, project, or provenance are not defined.
open_points.question: What scopes a payment identity, and how does the API handle a replay whose content differs?
options: Payment identity is global and differing replay is an integrity conflict
Payment identity is project-scoped and differing replay is a conflict
A repeated identity updates the existing payment
open_points.default_guess: Make the identity project-scoped and reject different content as an integrity conflict.

witness.initial: Payment identity PAY-1 records EUR 1,000 for project P.
events: An operator submits PAY-1 again for EUR 1,500.
outcomes: The existing EUR 1,000 result is returned without indicating the difference.
The request is rejected as an idempotency conflict.

open_points.subject: Derived actual-material totals
open_points.text: “Actual materials” and “remaining materials” are declared recomputable, but the text does not specify which expense amounts, inclusion state, allocation destinations, or material/work portions enter each section total.
open_points.question: What exact owning records and fields form actual materials and remaining materials, including Other expenses and unmapped allocations?
options: Sum included confirmed allocations to each budget section only
Sum every included expense allocated to a section regardless of expense category
Include Other expenses or unmapped amounts in project-level actual materials
open_points.default_guess: Sum only included confirmed allocation amounts assigned to the section; expose Other and unmapped amounts separately.

witness.initial: An included EUR 100 expense is allocated entirely to Other expenses.
events: A viewer requests the budget summary.
outcomes: Actual materials increases by EUR 100 at project level.
Actual materials is unchanged and EUR 100 appears only under Other expenses.

open_points.subject: Audit of first-administrator creation
open_points.text: R0-07 says first-administrator creation is “never … audited,” while the product invariant says “Every significant action carries actor provenance to audit” and administration audit includes staff-account actions.
open_points.question: Is bootstrap administrator creation an explicit exception to the audit invariant, or must it create an audit record with a host/deployment actor?
options: Bootstrap is deliberately unaudited
Bootstrap writes an audit record naming a deployment actor
Bootstrap writes a non-product operational security log only
open_points.default_guess: Treat bootstrap as an explicit documented exception to product audit and require a protected operational record outside the product audit.

witness.initial: The deployment has no staff accounts.
events: The host operator successfully creates the first administrator with the local command.
An auditor inspects all product audit records.
outcomes: No record exists, as R0-07 requires.
A bootstrap staff-creation record exists, as the audit invariant requires.

open_points.subject: Audit of failed and denied actions
open_points.text: “Every significant action records … result,” but it is not stated whether authorization denials, validation failures, idempotent replays, integrity conflicts, and external-system failures are actions that must be recorded.
open_points.question: Which attempted actions produce audit records, and what closed result values are recorded?
options: Audit every authenticated attempt including failures
Audit only state-changing successes
Audit successes plus a named subset of security and integrity failures
open_points.default_guess: Audit successes and all authenticated authorization, integrity, and security-relevant failures, with a closed result taxonomy.

witness.initial: An operator is authenticated but not assigned to project P.
events: The operator attempts to exclude an expense in P.
outcomes: A denied audit record is written with actor and project.
No audit record is written because no business state changed.

open_points.subject: Physical storage decision
open_points.text: Persistent data says “physical storage undecided at this state,” while R0-10 decides “one SQLite database file and one local directory.”
open_points.question: Is SQLite plus a local binary root part of the accepted State 0 product boundary, or is physical storage still open for a later state?
options: R0-10 settles physical storage in State 0
Storage remains open and R0-10 is nonbinding migration history
open_points.default_guess: R0-10 settles it: one SQLite database and one local binary root.

witness.initial: A later agent begins persistence design from this document.
events: The agent selects a persistence implementation.
outcomes: The agent must use SQLite and a local directory.
The agent may choose another database and object store because storage is declared undecided.

open_points.subject: Registry failure translation
open_points.text: The Registry boundary promises “typed failure translation,” but neither Registry failure kinds nor their portal-visible translations are named.
open_points.question: What does each Registry not-found, archived, unavailable, timeout, malformed-response, and identity-mismatch condition become for reads and writes?
options: Define a closed portal error for each Registry failure class
Hide all Registry failures behind one unavailable result
Translate not-found and archived separately while collapsing operational failures
open_points.default_guess: Define separate not-found, archived/read-only, and dependency-unavailable errors while hiding dependency internals.

witness.initial: A staff member is authorized for project P, but Registry times out during validation.
events: The staff member submits an expense for P.
outcomes: The portal returns a dependency-unavailable failure suitable for retry.
The portal reports P as not found or unauthorized.

open_points.subject: Email gateway delivery contract
open_points.text: The gateway “only delivers messages,” and delivery records are persistent, but the send request, accepted/rejected output, retry behavior, and effect of temporary or permanent delivery failure are not specified.
open_points.question: What observable states and actions govern queued, delivered, temporarily failed, and permanently failed staff email?
options: Synchronous gateway acceptance with explicit retryable failure
Persisted outbox with asynchronous attempts and status
Best-effort synchronous delivery without retry
open_points.default_guess: Use a persisted outbox/delivery record with explicit attempt status and retryable versus terminal failure.

witness.initial: An administrator creates a pending staff account and issues verification.
events: The email gateway is unavailable.
outcomes: The action succeeds with a pending delivery that will be retried.
The whole issuance fails and no usable challenge remains.

open_points.subject: Bootstrap command input and outputs
open_points.text: R0-07 says email and password are read neither from arguments, environment, nor a file, and that the outcome is “a closed set of exit codes,” but it names neither the remaining input channel nor the exit-code set.
open_points.question: How are bootstrap inputs supplied, and what exact exit codes distinguish success, existing staff, invalid input, configuration failure, and persistence failure?
options: Interactive terminal prompts with enumerated exit codes
Standard input protocol with enumerated exit codes
Platform-specific secret input channel
open_points.default_guess: Use non-echoing interactive terminal prompts and enumerate stable exit codes for success, already initialized, invalid input, configuration failure, and storage failure.

witness.initial: An empty deployment is being initialized by an automated deployment script.
events: The script invokes the bootstrap command and receives exit code 1.
outcomes: Code 1 means staff already exists and deployment may continue.
Code 1 means invalid configuration or database failure and deployment must stop.

open_points.subject: Sole-administrator recovery
open_points.text: R0-20 says “Recovery of the sole administrator stays a deployment-level operation (R0-07),” but R0-07 defines only first-account creation and requires refusal once any staff account exists.
open_points.question: What deployment-level action recovers an existing sole administrator, and what authority, inputs, output, and audit behavior does it have?
options: A separate local recovery command replaces the sole administrator email or credential
The bootstrap command gains a recovery mode
No recovery action exists once the first account has been created
open_points.default_guess: Define a separate local, interactive, heavily recorded recovery command restricted to the sole-administrator condition.

witness.initial: One active administrator exists, but its email account and password are inaccessible.
events: The host operator invokes the R0-07 command.
outcomes: Recovery succeeds because R0-20 refers to R0-07 as the deployment recovery path.
The command refuses because a staff account already exists, leaving no recovery path.

open_points.subject: Health-check output and readiness meaning
open_points.text: The service promises unauthenticated “liveness and readiness” answers, but does not define their routes, response shapes/statuses, or which dependencies and storage conditions make readiness fail.
open_points.question: What exactly do liveness and readiness return, and which checks determine each result?
options: Liveness tests only the process; readiness tests configuration, database, and binary root
Readiness also requires Registry and email gateway availability
Both endpoints report only process availability
open_points.default_guess: Use fixed non-sensitive responses; liveness checks the process, while readiness checks validated configuration, writable database access, and readable binary root but not optional remote dependency availability.

witness.initial: The process and SQLite database are healthy, but Registry is unavailable.
events: An orchestrator calls readiness.
outcomes: Readiness succeeds because local serving capacity is intact.
Readiness fails because a required external dependency is unavailable.

open_points.subject: Protected-binary media types
open_points.text: R0-12 requires media type to be “on a closed list per object kind,” but neither closed list is given.
open_points.question: Which detected media types are allowed for ExpenseDocument and ProgressPhoto?
options: A separately enumerated list for documents and photos
One shared allowlist
Deployment-configured allowlists
open_points.default_guess: Define immutable contract-level allowlists separately for documents and photos.

witness.initial: An authorized expense document contains valid PDF bytes.
events: The viewer downloads the document.
outcomes: The bytes are returned because PDF is allowed.
The request receives the indistinguishable read failure because PDF was not included in an implementer-selected list.

open_points.subject: Indistinguishable binary-read failure
open_points.text: “An unknown, cross-project, hidden, oversize or unlisted read is answered the same way,” but the common HTTP status, headers, and body are not stated.
open_points.question: What exact response represents every concealed binary-read failure?
options: 404 with a fixed empty body
404 with a fixed JSON error
403 with a fixed empty body
open_points.default_guess: Return a fixed 404 response with no object-specific headers or details.

witness.initial: Viewer V may read project P but document D is hidden.
events: V requests D.
V requests a nonexistent document identifier.
outcomes: Both requests return the same fixed 404 response.
Both are concealed but implementations choose different status or body details, revealing which condition occurred.

open_points.subject: PresuPro transport decision status
open_points.text: The unresolved list says the PresuPro transport is “Decided by R0-09: a bearer header,” while Open questions says “Still open … the PresuPro transport binding”; R0-09 says producers authenticate “only with a bearer header.”
open_points.question: Is the PresuPro transport binding closed as bearer authentication or intentionally still open?
options: Closed: producer requests use a bearer header
Open: bearer is only one candidate pending a later decision
open_points.default_guess: Treat it as closed by R0-09: bearer header only.

witness.initial: A producer integration is being implemented.
events: The producer sends a mutually authenticated request without a bearer header.
outcomes: The request is rejected because bearer-only transport is decided.
The request may be accepted because transport binding remains open.

open_points.subject: Currency rounding scope
open_points.text: Currency policy says “domain-defined rounding,” while R0-05 supplies “rounded half up to two places” without saying whether rounding occurs on every input, allocation, multiplication, section subtotal, or only final displayed totals.
open_points.question: At which calculation and validation boundaries is half-up two-decimal rounding applied, especially for splits and completed-work multiplication?
options: Quantize every stored money amount and each calculated component
Keep higher precision internally and round only exposed totals
Define operation-specific rounding points
open_points.default_guess: Store money at two decimals, calculate percentages at higher precision, and round each exposed monetary result half up to two decimals with explicit reconciliation rules.

witness.initial: A EUR 100.00 expense is manually split into three equal allocations.
events: The operator submits three percentage-equivalent parts.
outcomes: The portal stores 33.33, 33.33, and 33.34 so the sum remains EUR 100.00.
The portal computes three 33.33 amounts and rejects the split or loses EUR 0.01.

open_points.subject: Audit actor for unauthenticated actions
open_points.text: Audit requires a principal “user_id, viewer, or service principal,” while R0-15 permits unauthenticated password-reset requests, confirmations, viewer entry, and health checks; the audit actor representation for significant unauthenticated security actions is not named.
open_points.question: How are unauthenticated but security-relevant actions represented in audit without inventing a principal or leaking account existence?
options: Use an explicit anonymous/external actor kind
Record the targeted principal only after a token proves authority
Do not audit unauthenticated attempts
open_points.default_guess: Use an explicit anonymous actor kind for requests and attach a target entity only when doing so is safe internally.

witness.initial: An unknown caller requests a password reset for an existing staff email.
events: The portal accepts the enumeration-safe request.
outcomes: An audit record is written with an anonymous actor and protected target reference.
No audit record is possible because the listed actor types require an authenticated principal.

open_points.subject: Recovery-override email collision
open_points.text: R0-20 replaces the login email “with a given address” while staff email must be uniquely normalized; no outcome is stated when the address already belongs to another account or normalizes to one.
open_points.question: How does recovery override handle a duplicate or normalization-colliding email address?
options: Reject atomically with an explicit conflict
Transfer the address from the other account
Disable or rename the other account as part of recovery
open_points.default_guess: Reject atomically with a non-enumerating conflict visible only to the authorized administrator.

witness.initial: Staff accounts A and B exist; B owns normalized email x@example.com.
events: An administrator performs recovery override on A using X@example.com.
outcomes: The override fails and neither account changes.
A acquires the address and B is altered or left with a duplicate login.
witness.observer: The administrator and both account holders
